natural: I am grateful for your kind regard

meaning.en: A humble thanks for someone's generous favour, support or affection.
meaning.zh: 谦虚地感谢对方的厚待、关照或喜爱。

equivalents: thank you for your kind favour
I am honoured by your kindness

examples.zh: 承蒙厚爱，我一定不辜负大家的期望。
examples.en: I am grateful for your kind regard and will not let you down.

examples.zh: 多年来承蒙厚爱，本店特推出会员回馈活动。
examples.en: After years of your generous support, our shop is launching a loyalty offer.

usage.en: 谦辞 (humble expression): the speaker thanks others for their favour. Formal, used in speeches, letters and shop notices.
usage.zh: 谦辞：说话人感谢对方的厚待。正式，常见于致辞、信函和商家告示。

natural: please forgive me for not seeing you far

meaning.en: A polite or sometimes pointed formula said by a host when a guest leaves, excusing oneself from walking them out.
meaning.zh: 主人送客时的客套话，表示不再远送。

equivalents: forgive me for not seeing you out
I won't see you to the door

examples.en: Take care on the road; forgive me for not seeing you further.

examples.zh: 既然话不投机，恕不远送。
examples.en: Since we clearly disagree, I will not see you out.

usage.en: 谦辞 (humble) from the host. In old novels and modern banter it can sound curt or sarcastic, meaning 'there's the door'. Formal or humorous.
usage.zh: 主人的谦辞。在旧小说和现代调侃中有时带逐客的意味，显得冷淡或讽刺。正式或戏谑。

natural: mind how you go, I won't see you out

meaning.en: A casual farewell from the host, often meaning 'go carefully; I won't walk you out'.
meaning.zh: 主人送客的口语告别语，意为“路上慢点，我就不送了”。

equivalents: take care, I won't see you out

examples.en: All right, mind how you go; I won't see you out.

examples.zh: 她笑着对要走的同事说：“慢走不送！”
examples.en: She smiled at the colleague who was leaving and said, 'Off you go, then!'

usage.en: Friendly between close people, but said sharply it means 'good riddance'. Tone decides the meaning. Casual.
usage.zh: 亲近的人之间是客气话，语气冷淡时则有“快走吧”的意思，全看语气。口语。

meaning.en: The standard greeting of shops, restaurants and hotels to arriving customers.
meaning.zh: 商店、餐馆、酒店对来客的标准问候语。

examples.zh: 店员微笑着说：“欢迎光临！”
门口的牌子上写着“欢迎光临”。
examples.en: The sign at the door reads 'Welcome'.

usage.en: 敬辞: 光临 honours the visitor's arrival. Used by businesses and hosts; customers do not say it back. Neutral, standard on signs.
usage.zh: 敬辞：“光临”是敬称对方到来。多由商家或主人说，顾客不回答此语。中性，招牌常用。

natural: please honour my humble home with a visit

meaning.en: A humble invitation asking someone to visit one's home.
meaning.zh: 谦虚地邀请对方到自己家中做客。

equivalents: do honour my house with a visit

examples.zh: 改日定当请您光临寒舍。
examples.en: I shall invite you to honour my humble home one day.

examples.zh: 盼老师有空光临寒舍小坐。
examples.en: I hope you will find time to visit my humble home, teacher.

usage.en: Mixes 敬辞 光临 (for the guest) and 谦辞 寒舍 (for one's own home). Formal, slightly old-fashioned, often humorous today.
usage.zh: “光临”是敬辞，“寒舍”是谦辞，合起来用。正式，略显古雅，今天常带玩笑口吻。

natural: forgive me for not welcoming you properly

meaning.en: A humble apology from a host for not greeting a guest at the door or from afar.
meaning.zh: 主人对客人表示没有远道迎接的歉意。

equivalents: forgive me for not meeting you
sorry I did not come out to greet you

examples.zh: 不知您大驾光临，有失远迎，还请见谅。
examples.en: I did not know you were coming, and forgive me for failing to greet you properly.
Mr Wang is here? Forgive me for not meeting you!

usage.en: 谦辞 (humble) said by the host on meeting a guest. Formal; heard in period dramas and ceremonious or jokey modern speech.
usage.zh: 主人见客时说的谦辞。正式，古装剧中常听到，今天也用于郑重或玩笑场合。

meaning.en: A humble apology for a lapse in manners, in the style of old fiction.
meaning.zh: 旧小说式的谦辞，为自己的失礼道歉。

examples.zh: 方才多喝了几杯，在下失礼了。
examples.en: I had a few too many just now; forgive my rudeness.

examples.zh: 他拱手道：“在下失礼，诸位莫怪。”
examples.en: He bowed with clasped hands and said, 'Pardon my manners, gentlemen.'

usage.en: 谦辞 with 在下 ('the one below') for 'I'. Literary, from period dramas and martial-arts novels; used playfully today.
usage.zh: 谦辞，“在下”是自称。带文言色彩，多见于古装剧和武侠小说，现今多用于玩笑。

natural: I have given offence on many occasions

meaning.en: A humble apology for having offended someone more than once.
meaning.zh: 谦虚地为自己多次冒犯对方道歉。

equivalents: I may have offended you often

examples.zh: 以前多有得罪，请您大人不记小人过。
examples.en: I offended you many times before; please be generous and forget it.

examples.zh: 交接工作中多有得罪，还望海涵。
examples.en: I may have stepped on toes during the handover; I hope you will forgive me.

usage.en: 谦辞 (humble): usually spoken at partings, ends of projects or toasts. Often followed by 还请海涵. Formal.
usage.zh: 谦辞：多用于离别、项目结束或敬酒时，后面常接“还请海涵”。正式。

meaning.en: A polite request for patience and forgiveness for one's shortcomings.
meaning.zh: 客气地请对方对自己的不足多加谅解。

examples.zh: 我刚学汉语，说得不好，请多包涵。
examples.en: I've only just started Chinese and speak badly, so please bear with me.

examples.zh: 今天准备仓促，有不周之处，请多包涵。
examples.en: The preparations were hasty and there are shortcomings; please bear with us.

usage.en: 谦辞 (humble): spoken by the one at fault or the host. Also written 多多包涵; 包涵 alone means 'to forgive'. Neutral, polite.
usage.zh: 谦辞：由有不足的一方或主人说，也说“多多包涵”；单说“包涵”即“原谅”。中性，礼貌。
